recorded_uses.name: Garlic
recorded_uses.pros: Food-grade herb; trials and reviews report a small fall in blood pressure.
recorded_uses.cons: The fall is modest; smell and stomach upset are common complaints.
recorded_uses.cautions: Adds to blood-pressure medicines and raises bleeding risk with blood thinners.
recorded_uses.source_note: PMID 11834913 (review of herbs and supplements in cardiovascular disease)
recorded_uses.uses: Classical use of lashuna for circulatory complaints.

recorded_uses.name: Garlic
recorded_uses.pros: Reviews report small improvements in blood pressure and in cholesterol.
recorded_uses.cons: No proof that it prevents heart attacks or strokes; the effects are modest.
recorded_uses.cautions: Raises bleeding risk alongside antiplatelet and anticoagulant medicines.
recorded_uses.uses: Classical use of lashuna for circulatory complaints.
recorded_uses.condition_name: Prevention of a further heart attack or stroke

recorded_uses.name: Garlic
recorded_uses.pros: Laboratory and animal work shows reduced platelet clumping.
recorded_uses.cons: No evidence that it prevents or treats a clot in people.
recorded_uses.cautions: Does not replace an anticoagulant; taken with one, bleeding risk rises markedly.
recorded_uses.source_note: PMID 11834913 and PMID 13678230 (platelet and antithrombotic activity); warfarin interaction curator-confirmed in this project (PMID 10675182)
recorded_uses.uses: Classical use of lashuna as a warming herb that moves the blood.
recorded_uses.condition_name: Blood clot in a vein (DVT or pulmonary embolism)

recorded_uses.name: Garlic
recorded_uses.pros: Common food; animal studies report modest falls in blood glucose.
recorded_uses.cons: The effect on sugar is small and inconsistent in people; strong smell.
recorded_uses.cautions: Raises bleeding risk with blood thinners; a documented warfarin interaction exists.
recorded_uses.source_note: PMID 16801983 (glycaemic); warfarin interaction curator-confirmed in this project (PMID 10675182, 19719333, 21919844)
recorded_uses.uses: Classical use of lashuna as a warming herb for vata and circulatory complaints.
